name: Unpacking Checklist
description: A room-by-room unpacking checklist for the first days in a new home, starting with essentials and finishing with box breakdown and admin.

items.text: Walk through the home and check for damage before unpacking
Confirm electricity, water, heating and internet are working
Test smoke and carbon monoxide alarms
Find the main water shutoff and the electrical panel
Change or rekey the locks if possible
items.note: Previous owners, tenants or contractors may still have keys.

items.text: Check every box and furniture piece arrived against your inventory
Unpack the first-night box: chargers, medication, toiletries and a change of clothes
Assemble and make the beds
Put up curtains or temporary covers in bedrooms
Set out towels, toilet paper, soap and a shower curtain
Keep snacks, water and basic tools within reach
Wipe out cabinets, drawers and the fridge before filling them
Unpack plates, cups, cutlery and one pot and pan first
Set up the kettle, coffee maker and other daily appliances
Store everyday items near where you use them
Put cleaning products out of reach of children and pets
Clean the bathroom before unpacking
Unpack toiletries, towels and the medicine cabinet
Keep medications stored safely and out of reach
Unpack clothes for the next week first
Hang clothes and fill drawers
Set up the children's rooms early to help them settle
Place large furniture before unpacking smaller items
Set up the TV, Wi-Fi router and work-from-home desk
Unpack books, decor and pictures last
Sort the garage, shed and storage areas
Anchor tall furniture and TVs to the wall if you have children
items.note: Tip-overs of furniture and TVs are a leading cause of home injuries to young children.

items.text: Flatten boxes as you empty them
Check packing paper for small items before throwing it away
Recycle, store or give away boxes and packing materials
Note any damaged items and file mover's claims promptly
Update your address with banks, employer, insurer and subscriptions
Register with local services such as a doctor, dentist and vet

faq.q: What should you unpack first after moving?
faq.a: Unpack your first-night box, bedding and bathroom essentials first, then the kitchen basics you need to eat. These make the home livable on day one. Decor, books and items for storage can wait until the main rooms work.

faq.q: How long does it take to unpack after a move?
faq.a: Most households unpack the essentials in one to three days and finish everything in one to two weeks. Setting a daily target, such as two rooms or a fixed number of boxes, stops the last few boxes sitting untouched for months.

faq.q: Which room should you unpack first?
faq.a: Start with the bedrooms' beds and the bathroom so everyone can sleep and wash, then the kitchen. The living room usually comes next, with the garage, spare room and storage areas last.

faq.q: What should you do with moving boxes after unpacking?
faq.a: Flatten boxes as you empty them and either store a few for future use, give them away to someone moving, or recycle them. Remove packing paper and bubble wrap promptly, since piles of it make it easy to throw away small items by mistake.
